title: Partner listing — security gates, asset retirement & acceptance checklist (draft)
content:
Purpose
-----
This is a working draft that consolidates checklist items and copy fragments for partner marketplace listings where we need to: 1) verify security and compliance gates, 2) define a process for deprecating partner-provided assets (tiles, icons, screenshots, artifacts), and 3) produce final acceptance criteria for go-to-market signoff. The goal is to reduce last-minute rework at publication and to make clear the responsibilities across GTM, Legal, Security, and Engineering.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all third-party and partner product listings in cloud marketplaces (AWS, Azure, GCP, and select channel stores).
- Focus on the intersection of marketing copy assets (tile, short/long descriptions), technical acceptance (deploy/test matrix), security controls (data residency, KMS, SSO), and asset lifecycle (replacement/retirement).
- Does NOT attempt to replace vendor-specific legal contracts; instead, flags where Legal must be engaged.

Audience and stakeholders
-----------------------
- Primary owner: Partner GTM lead (owner listed in partner intake).
- Redwood reviewers: go-to-market listing owner (Aisha Kaur), Security reviewer (Daniel Ortiz), Solutions Eng (Maya Thompson), Billing/org ops (Luca Romano), Legal reviewer (Priya Malhotra).
- Eng & SRE contacts to validate technical prerequisites: eng-dedicated, eng-private-deployments on intake ticket.

High-level checklist (quick pass)
--------------------------------
1) Copy readiness
   - Tile headline (<= 60 chars) prepared + approved by partner and Redwood messaging.
   - Short description (150–250 chars) focused on primary use-case and top-two differentiators.
   - Long description (400–1,000 chars) with feature bullets, integrations, required infra.
   - 3–5 screenshots + 1 architecture diagram (PNG/SVG), all labelled with version and date.
   - One-sentence elevator pitch for listing tile used in promo banners.

2) Security & compliance gates
   - Data residency declared and supported (yes/no + list of regions).
   - KMS/HSM integration: partner must confirm encryption-at-rest approach and key lifecycle.
   - SSO/SAML/OIDC: verify compatibility and provide test account for SSO end-to-end test.
   - Network egress characteristics documented (outbound IPs/ranges if applicable).
   - Privacy & PII handling statement included.
   - Vulnerability disclosure and incident contact info provided.

3) Billing & metering
   - SKU mapping suggested by partner + Redwood internal SKU proposal.
   - Trial/quota parameters for marketplace trial tile (trial length, token limits, free tier).
   - Billing tests: provisioning->metering->invoice cycle validated in sandbox.

4) Technical prerequisites
   - Test harness: partner provides a reproducible demo script and API key/test tenant.
   - Deploy matrix: supported runtimes/versions, min hardware (GPU/CPU), quantization profiles if relevant.
   - API contract: sample requests/responses, rate limit expectations.
   - Observability hooks: tracing/span ids, error codes, op-level metrics mapping.

5) Asset lifecycle & deprecation policy (new section)
   - Each asset (tile, screenshot, architecture image, whitepaper PDF) must include a published version string and a deprecation date field (optional at publication, required for major versioned assets).
   - Deprecation notice workflow: 60/30/7 day notifications to partner and Redwood GTM for removal or replacement.
   - Emergency removal: Security or Legal can request immediate takedown; listing owner must ack within 24 hours and provide remediation plan within 72 hours.
   - Archive location: partner must supply a public or restricted archive link for older assets if customers request historic artifacts.

Acceptance criteria (detailed)
-----------------------------
- Copy: final tile + short + long descriptions approved in writing by Partner GTM and Redwood messaging (Slack thread or signed doc).
- Security: security reviewer (Daniel Ortiz) records checklist signoff and attaches short remediation plan for any outstanding low-severity issues (must be resolved before public listing).
- Billing: Billing owner (Luca) confirms sandbox metering and that the SKU maps to internal revenue codes.
- Tech: Solutions Eng (Maya) verifies demo script runs end-to-end in Redwood test environment and captures smoke-test logs.
- Legal: any claims flagged as regulated (healthcare, finance) must have legal signoff before launch.

Copy fragments (working, fill-in-the-blanks)
-------------------------------------------
- Tile headline (example): "Deploy fast LLM inference for customer-facing apps"
- Short description (example): "Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments for low-latency LLM inference with predictable costs and production observability."
- Long description bullets (example):
  • Unified API for text generation, embeddings, and reranking.
  • Dedicated GPU pools and autoscaling for throughput-sensitive workloads.
  • Private VPC & on-prem connectors for regulated data.
  • Built-in cost/latency dashboards and rollout controls.
- Promotional one-liner for tile banner: "Lower inference costs, maintain SLAs — ship LLM features with confidence."

Technical test cases (sample)
-----------------------------
- Smoke test: deploy sample app using partner sample API key -> generate 128-token completion within SLA (<= 300ms p95 depending on model).
- SSO test: IdP-initiated login -> scoped token minted -> API call authorized.
- Billing test: start trial, call endpoints to consume 1k tokens, verify usage shows in sandbox metering within 30 minutes.
- Failover test: simulate region outage -> listing fallback to alternate region works and no customer-facing errors for 95% of requests.

Asset retirement example flow (scenario)
-------------------------------------
- Reason: Partner changes UI screenshots after major UX rev.
- Partner uploads replacement assets to shared artifact bucket and tags as v2.0.
- Partner sets deprecation date for v1.0 assets 45 days out.
- Redwood GTM schedules replacement: staging validation (7 days), approval by messaging (3 days), and public swap on day 45.
- If any security issue discovered with v1.0: immediate takedown and rollback plan executed; customers notified per incident policy.

Operational runbook notes (short)
--------------------------------
- Preflight: complete checklist at least 10 business days before planned publish.
- Dry run: schedule a dry run publish in sandbox; must be green for security, billing, and smoke tests.
- Launch day: GTM on-call, Eng on-call, Security on-call, and Billing on-call present in a single Slack channel for first 3 hours.
- Post-launch 48h review: collect telemetry anomaly signals and partner feedback; file follow-up tickets for any regressions.

Open questions / TODOs
---------------------
- How strictly do we enforce deprecation dates for marketing collateral vs. technical artifacts? (Proposal: marketing assets get soft enforcement with notifications; technical artifacts require hard retirement per policy.)
- Confirm where archived assets live (S3 bucket vs. partner-hosted). Add governance notes.
- Should we add automated expiry metadata into the listing manifest so marketplace UI can show "soon to be retired" flags? (Engineering input needed).
- Define SLA for partner responsiveness during emergency takedown (suggestion: 24 hours).

Next steps & owners
-------------------
- Finalize copy snippets and publish to partner draft: Owner Aisha Kaur (by 2026-02-28).
- Security checklist formalization: Owner Daniel Ortiz (draft to security playbook, due 2026-03-05).
- Add automated 'deprecation' field to listing manifest spec: Eng-Console (ticket ENG-CONS-412, due 2026-03-18).
- Confirm billing SKU mapping in sandbox with partner: Owner Luca Romano (complete by 2026-03-01).

Notes and references (internal links)
-----------------------------------
- See intake template: CONFLUENCE-1234 (partner intake).
- Example ticket for prior listing with emergency takedown: JIRA-SEC-991.
- Related GTM checklist that covers promos and co-marketing: CONFLUENCE-GTM-88.

Quick appendix: minimal publish checklist (for last-minute sanity)
----------------------------------------------------------------
- [ ] Tile headline approved
- [ ] Short description approved
- [ ] 1 architecture diagram included
- [ ] Security signoff recorded
- [ ] Billing mapped to internal SKU and trial parameters set
- [ ] Demo script passes smoke in sandbox
- [ ] Deprecation fields present for any versioned asset
- [ ] Launch channel set (Slack + pager duty)

Version history
---------------
- 2025-11-03: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2025-12-12: added asset retirement flow & deprecation policy (Maya)
- 2026-02-20: security gate clarifications and operational runbook additions (Daniel)

Document status: working draft — expect incremental changes as Engineering and Security formalize the manifest schema and archive locations.

Unstructured notes (scratch / handoff)
------------------------------------
- If partner asks for a faster publish window, require a documented mitigation plan for any missing non-critical items (e.g., missing optional screenshots).
- Consider adding a small badge/CTA in tile metadata for "supports private deployments" to clarify offering without bloating copy.
- Keep evidence (signed approvals, smoke logs) attached to the intake ticket for audit traces.
file_notes: Working doc intended to be used by GTM + Security + Eng for partner marketplace listings; do not distribute externally until labelled final.
